title: Rejoice not (Avot 4:19, Proverbs 24:17)
hook: a group chat laughing at someone's fall: Shmuel the Small taught "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth"
tomorrow: learning young or learning old: which one actually sticks?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: don't calm a friend at the height of anger, or comfort while the loss is fresh. Timing is kindness. Today, the moment after someone falls.

The clip is already going around. Someone's big moment went wrong, and the group chat is doing what group chats do: the replays, the jokes, the crying-laughing faces. And she isn't even a friend. She's the one who beat you. Do you laugh too? A sage called Shmuel the Small answered with a single verse, and it's the whole of his saying in Avot.
screen: `THE CLIP IS GOING AROUND.` → `SHE'S THE ONE WHO BEAT YOU.` → `DO YOU LAUGH TOO?`

segments.voice: Shmuel the Small doesn't write anything new. His entire teaching in Avot is a quotation from Proverbs: "Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth." And don't let your heart be glad when he stumbles. The next verse gives a reason: lest the Lord see it, and it displease him. That's one to tell a friend tonight: a sage whose whole saying is somebody else's verse, and it asks a lot. Not a friend. An enemy. Not a stranger's fall. A rival's. Rejoice not. Now the week, because it's all here. Not in our hands: you can't explain why she got the slot. Greet first: say hi anyway. The corridor: get ready where no one sees. One hour here: use it to make something right. And timing is kindness: wait for the moment. Put them together and Shmuel's verse is what's left. Rejoice not.
screen: `HIS WHOLE SAYING IS A VERSE.` · `REJOICE NOT WHEN THINE ENEMY FALLETH.` · `AN ENEMY, NOT A FRIEND.` · `THE WEEK, IN SIX SAYINGS.` · then, large: `REJOICE NOT.`

segments.voice: With a pen, write the first name of someone whose stumble you'd be tempted to enjoy. Under it, write one ordinary thing you hope goes right for them this week. Leave the page face down, and rest for the rest of the sit.
screen: `ONE NAME.` · `ONE THING THAT GOES RIGHT FOR THEM.` · `PAGE FACE DOWN.`
